text:
Recent work supports testing recommender correctness beyond ranking accuracy. A [2024 empirical study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) develops metamorphic relations and evaluates LibRec, PREA and Surprise: output relationships can reveal failures without known correct recommendations. [ICLR 2024 activation-patching research](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Hf17y6u9BC) finds localization results sensitive to corruption methods and scoring metrics. These support a controlled diagnostic toolkit, but do not establish NextItNet-specific detection sensitivity or runtime.

For NextItNet, derive structural controls from its [causal dilated-convolution architecture](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf). Proposed tests: perturb future tokens and verify earlier features remain unchanged; compare identical histories with extra left padding, where supported; verify readout against the final nonpadding index; perturb history at different lags. Compute receptive-field reach from every actual convolution, including both convolutions within residual blocks. Changes outside that reach should have no effect; weak effects inside it indicate limited measured context use, not necessarily an implementation fault. Temporary positive-control faults can introduce future-token access, disable padding masks, select count−1, or suppress contextual convolution branches. Negative controls include identity hooks and perturbations outside causal reach.

For localization, cache clean block activations, corrupt one history region, then restore individual block outputs and measure recovery of fixed target-versus-negative score margins. Include reverse patching, identity patches and matched unrelated-history controls; recovery alone does not prove a unique mechanism. Report detection sensitivity across injected faults, false-alarm rate on clean controls, injected-block localization accuracy, confidence intervals, forward-pass counts and synchronized GPU runtime. These are proposed measurements—not published NextItNet results—and require only temporary interventions on each category’s existing checkpoint.
